name: India ↔ Southeast Asia Maritime Route
genZNote: This is the sea-route version of India's 'Act East' policy — you can't pivot east without an actual sea lane to do it through.

sections.heading: 🛳️ Route Path
bullets: India's east-coast ports (Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata) → Bay of Bengal → Andaman Sea (past India's Andaman & Nicobar Islands) → Strait of Malacca → South China Sea / Southeast Asian ports (Singapore, Port Klang, Ho Chi Minh City, Bangkok).
India's Andaman & Nicobar Islands sit close to this route's western approach to the Strait of Malacca.

sections.heading: 📦 Why It Matters
bullets: The maritime backbone of India's trade with ASEAN countries — machinery, textiles, pharmaceuticals and agricultural products move along it, alongside electronics and manufactured goods moving toward India.
Central to India's 'Act East' policy, which aims to deepen economic and strategic ties with Southeast and East Asia.
Also connects onward toward East Asia (China, Japan, South Korea) via the South China Sea, making it relevant to India's broader Indo-Pacific trade.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The India-Southeast Asia route runs from India's east coast through the Bay of Bengal and Strait of Malacca to ASEAN ports, underpinning India's Act East trade policy.
keyFacts: Path: India's east coast → Bay of Bengal → Strait of Malacca → Southeast Asia.
Andaman & Nicobar Islands sit near this route's western approach.
commonConfusion: This route uses India's EAST coast (Bay of Bengal side) — don't mix it up with the west-coast Gulf route.

highYieldFacts: India-Southeast Asia route passes through the Strait of Malacca.
Key Indian ports: Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata.
commonTraps: Don't state this route bypasses the Strait of Malacca — it is the essential link along the way.
mustRemember: India-Southeast Asia route = Bay of Bengal + Malacca corridor underpinning Act East.
